correctness.rationale: The residue map is explicitly computed. Hensel’s lemma gives the unique fixed point in \(3+5\mathbb Z_5\); contraction of \(f^4\) on each of the four other residue balls gives the unique attracting 4-cycle. On \(B=3+5\mathbb Z_5\), \(f\) is an isometry. The congruences \(g'(\alpha)\equiv16\pmod{25}\) and \(g''(\alpha)\equiv0\pmod5\) imply \(\nu_5(g(x)-x)=k+1\) on every shell of depth \(k\). Taylor period lifting then gives exact period \(4\cdot5^{n-k-1}\), and the shell cardinality equals this period, proving one cycle and minimality. The finite script checks \(n=1,\ldots,5\) only; it does not replace the all-level proof.

value.rationale: This is a complete exact decomposition of a simple cubic p-adic polynomial outside the quadratic examples emphasized in the inspected literature. It distinguishes a basin of Haar measure 4/5 from an invariant ball of measure 1/5 containing one fixed point and countably many minimal shells, and it gives the exact period of every shell at every finite level. The second-derivative cancellation for the fourth return is the structural feature enabling the exact all-level period law; this is more than a finite table or a routine restatement of the general decomposition theorem.
